acceptance_criteria.criterion: For every admitted plain object, the encoder examines all own property descriptors rather than only enumerable keys.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: encodePlainObject uses Object.getOwnPropertyNames, Object.getOwnPropertySymbols, and Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor for each string-keyed own property.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A plain object with any non-enumerable own string-keyed data property causes CanonicalEncoderError.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: encodePlainObject checks descriptor.enumerable before reading descriptor.value and throws NON_ENUMERABLE_PROPERTY; tests 51, 53, 55, 57, and 62 cover direct and nested cases.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A plain object with any non-enumerable own string-keyed accessor property causes CanonicalEncoderError without invoking the accessor.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The enumerability check precedes the data/accessor distinction. Tests assert NON_ENUMERABLE_PROPERTY and zero getter/setter invocation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: ADR-009 explicitly states that non-enumerable own properties are unsupported and identifies CanonicalEncoderError as the required outcome.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: ADR-009 §5 explicitly rejects non-enumerable data and accessor properties with CanonicalEncoderError code NON_ENUMERABLE_PROPERTY.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing canonical bytes and ordering for supported values remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The accepted baseline reportedly contains no canonical encoder or ADR-009; this candidate introduces a 441-line encoder and a complete byte format. BLOCKER-0001 confirms that compatibility with an existing accepted encoding cannot be established under the task's amendment premise.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The submitted verification evidence includes the exact npm run compile command output and exit code 0.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The Implementer report records stdout lines '> ciclo@0.0.0 compile' and '> tsc -b tsconfig.json', empty stderr, and exit code 0.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All repository lint, architecture-boundary, compile, and test gates exit successfully.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The Implementer report records exit code 0 for compile, boundary, lint, and 99-test execution; automated validation independently confirms lint and 99/99 tests, and the test set includes boundary checks.

findings.evidence: SPEC_BLOCKERS.md records BLOCKER-0001 as OPEN and says Interpretation A—the interpretation implemented by this candidate—may only be accepted by the product owner. The same record states that the accepted baseline contains neither ADR-009 nor a CanonicalEncoder. Merely recording the contradiction does not authorize landing work that depends on one side of it.
findings.required_change: Obtain and record the required product-owner resolution under CICLO_SPEC.md §19 before resubmitting this candidate. If Interpretation B is selected, restore the candidate to the narrow amendment task after the prerequisite encoder/ADR state is accepted through the proper task sequence.
findings.title: Candidate depends on an unresolved TRAVADA interpretation

findings.evidence: Beyond non-enumerable-property rejection, the candidate creates the complete encoder and wire format, adds UNPAIRED_SURROGATE rejection across all string positions, changes admission of Array/Set/Map subclasses, adds package ESM configuration, and adds numerous tests for those rules. The original task excludes unrelated canonical-encoding changes and new byte-format work; BLOCKER-0001 acknowledges this is previously unaccepted scope.
findings.required_change: After resolving BLOCKER-0001, limit the submitted change to the authorized baseline and the enumerability correction. Remove surrogate handling, collection-subclass policy, and other encoder-introduction work unless the product-owner resolution explicitly authorizes that combined scope.
findings.title: Candidate contains material changes outside the narrow task scope

invariants_checked: INV-22 injectivity for admitted plain objects with hidden properties
Canonical byte distinction between supported type tags
Accessor rejection without getter or setter invocation
risks: Accepting an OPEN TRAVADA-dependent interpretation would silently choose a specification resolution reserved for the product owner.
The broad encoder and ADR would become the canonical foundation for future StateHash and SaveHash despite lacking authorized sequencing.
Unrelated supported-domain restrictions could constrain downstream state design without a task specifically authorizing those decisions.

unrelated_changes: Introduction of the complete CanonicalEncoder and canonical byte format into an accepted baseline that had no encoder
Exact-prototype rejection for Array, Set, and Map subclasses
packages/core ESM-mode change needed by the newly introduced encoder/test surface
Broad ADR-009 creation beyond the required non-enumerable-property amendment

payload.summary: The non-enumerable-property behavior is implemented and tested, but the candidate cannot become canonical while BLOCKER-0001 remains OPEN. It introduces the entire previously absent CanonicalEncoder and ADR-009, plus unrelated surrogate and collection-subclass rules, based on an interpretation that the blocker explicitly says requires product-owner resolution.
